precepts.text: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria. Samaria was the capital for Ephraim.
precepts.point: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him, and he abode there two days. If they weren't Israelites, why would he stay there and teach them for two days? It makes no sense. Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world: of the world of Israel.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Why is a woman of Samaria an Israelite, and why did the Jews have no dealings with her? Isaiah names it: “And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”. Samaria was the capital of Ephraim, the head city of the northern kingdom.

So when John says Christ “must needs go through Samaria” and met “a woman of Samaria”, he is in the land of Ephraim, among the northern kingdom. That is why she could say “our father Jacob, which gave us the well”, and “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. Her fathers were the fathers of Israel.

The rift between the kingdoms went back to Rehoboam, and Judah had nothing to do with Ephraim and its capital. But Christ said “the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”, the hour of 70 AD, when nobody would be worshipping in Jerusalem or Samaria. “Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” He stayed two days in Samaria and many believed on him. That is the raising up of the tabernacle of David that fell: both houses gathered back to the Messiah.

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken. It was already prophesied: God already told them that in 65 years the northern kingdom would be destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Before Hosea recorded the Lord casting off the house of Israel, Isaiah had already prophesied it: “For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

They already knew. God already told them that within sixty-five years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be broken and destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording: Lo–ruhamah, no more mercy on the house of Israel, and Lo–ammi, ye are not my people.

So when the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans, she is standing at the end of that prophecy. Ephraim was broken “that it be not a people”, cut off for idolatry. And that is exactly why it matters that Christ, a Jew, is speaking to her at Jacob's well: the people who were broken off are about to be offered the living water.

precepts.text: Two manner of nations my heart abhorreth, and the third is no nation: they that sit upon the mountain of Samaria, the Greeks who ruled it then, they that dwell among the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem. The foolish people of Shechem are the northern kingdom, 'no nation' and 'foolish,' exactly as Moses wrote.
precepts.point: Ephraim allied with Syria against Judah. The head of Syria is Damascus and the head of Damascus is Rezin, and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. That is who Moses meant by 'not a people.'

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Ephraim aligned itself with Syria to attack its own brother Judah, and Isaiah 7:8 is the prophecy against them for it. “For the head of Syria is Damascus”, Syria's capital, “and the head of Damascus is Rezin”, the king of the Syrians at that time, “and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” That is who Moses was talking about when he said the Lord would provoke Israel to jealousy with them which are not a people, with a foolish nation: Ephraim.

Sirach shows the same people by name and place. “There be two manner of nations which my heart abhorreth, and the third is no nation.” Two nations he despises, and the third is no nation at all. “They that sit upon the mountain of Samaria”: in this context that is the Greeks, who ruled over Samaria then, and he says he despises them. “And they that dwell among the Philistines”: the Philistines are Hamites, and he hates them too.

“And that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.” Foolish, and no nation: the very words Moses used, not a people and foolish. Who dwelt in Shechem? The northern kingdom. Shechem is in Samaria, northern kingdom's land, where Abraham built that altar. It is by Sychar, where Christ met the woman at the well, near “the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph”, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh.

So Isaiah says Ephraim would be broken that it be not a people, Hosea calls them Lo-ammi, not my people, and Sirach calls them no nation and foolish. It is the same people every time. And that is why Peter writes to “the strangers scattered” which “in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”: Christ laid down his life for the other sheep not of Judah's fold, to gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.

precepts.text: The Lord would be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.
precepts.point: Within sixty-five years Ephraim would be broken, that it be not a people. That phrase is the key to the whole class.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
In the days of Ahaz, Ephraim conspired with the Syrians to overthrow Judah: the Syro-Ephraimite war. Rezin was the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah was king of Ephraim, and their plan was to take Judah's land and set the son of Tabeal as king over it. Ahaz was weak and wicked, and his heart shook “as the trees of the wood are moved”. But the Lord said the counsel of Syria and Ephraim would not stand: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

In Isaiah 8 the Lord brings “the king of Assyria, and all his glory” like a river over his banks. Assyria would rise up and conquer Ephraim, and also pass through Judah and take some portions of it, but not fully like Ephraim. “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought” … “for God is with us.” Isaiah's sons were born as signs that Ephraim and Syria would be overthrown by Assyria and would not succeed against Judah.

So the Lord tells Isaiah not to fear their confederacy, and not to be like Ahaz, cowardly and weak: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.” It says both. The Lord speaks of one Israel as two houses: the house of Judah and the house of Ephraim, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. And that stone of stumbling is Christ.

He is “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem”, a trap to both houses, but specifically to those in Jerusalem. “And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” The context has not changed. Not only did Ephraim fall physically and spiritually; Judah fell physically and spiritually too, but worse, because they stumbled at that stone.

Hosea shows Ephraim's side. His daughter Lo-ruhamah, no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it be not a people. His son Lo-ammi: “for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, that makes you a Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read that and said, good, the hell with Ephraim, they are Gentiles, we don't deal with them anymore.

The rock ties it together. Moses said “He is the Rock, his work is perfect” … “a God of truth and without iniquity”, and “is not he thy father that hath bought thee?” That rock of Isaiah 8 is Christ, our God and our father, and the stone both houses of Israel stumbled over.

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim, head of the northern kingdom, be broken, that it be not a people.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people”. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel. No: the ones which are not a people are also Israel.

Isaiah says who: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” Ephraim, the head of the northern kingdom, was broken so that it be not a people. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. Those which are not a people are our own brothers and sisters, broken off for a dispensation of time.

precepts.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria; Ephraim became the ruler of the ten tribes.
precepts.point: Ephraim being greater goes into Ephraim becoming the head of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria; and it was Ephraim that led the charge, with the help of Issachar and Manasseh, that brought the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. The unicorn there is not a fairy tale horse; the original etymology goes into the rhinoceros.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

precepts.why:
“And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.” Israel said Ephraim, the younger brother, “shall be greater than he”, and here is where that goes: Ephraim became the ruler of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria.

The greatness Joshua speaks of, “Thou art a great people, and hast great power”, grew into Ephraim standing at the head of the northern kingdom.

precepts.text: In the days of Ahaz, Syria and Ephraim came up against Jerusalem but could not prevail; the Most High foretold that within threescore and five years Ephraim would be broken.
precepts.point: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, slew the king's son, the governor of the house, and the man next to the king. The children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand women, sons, and daughters, and much spoil, and brought it to Samaria. This was brother against brother, one nation of Israel captiving the other.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
It was “in the days of Ahaz” that “Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.” It was told the house of David, “Syria is confederate with Ephraim”, and the heart of Ahaz and his people was moved “as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.”

The Most High sent Isaiah to tell Ahaz, “Take heed, and be quiet; fear not”, for the evil counsel of Syria and Ephraim “shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.” He foretold that “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” And he warned, “If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.”

These are the same two kings in Chronicles. Because Judah “had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers”, the Most High delivered Ahaz “into the hand of the king of Syria”, who carried captives to Damascus, and “into the hand of the king of Israel”. “Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, which were all valiant men”. Zichri, “a mighty man of Ephraim”, slew the king’s son, the governor of the house and the man next to the king, and “the children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand” to Samaria. This was brother against brother, one nation of Israel captiving the other.

precepts.text: Isaiah and the children the Most High gave him are set for signs and wonders in Israel, dwelling in mount Zion.
precepts.point: The sign is the child, not the virgin herself. Many think the virgin was the sign, and that leads into all types of false doctrine; the virgin is simply a woman of age to be married. Captain OC opened how christianity stumbles over the word seed.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

precepts.why:
“Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” The sign is the child, not the virgin herself. Isaiah shows what a sign is in the next chapter: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.”

Isaiah and the children the Most High gave him are set for signs and wonders in Israel. The children are the signs. Many think the virgin was the sign, and that leads into all types of false doctrine; the virgin is simply a woman of age to be married. Captain OC opened how christianity stumbles over the word seed.

precepts.text: The capital of Ephraim is Samaria, proving Aholah/Samaria is the northern kingdom of Ephraim.
precepts.point: The elder is Aholah and her sister is Aholibah; they were the Most High's and bare sons and daughters. Aholah is Samaria, the northern kingdom, and Aholibah is Jerusalem, the southern kingdom.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
“Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah.” To know who Aholah is, you have to know whose city Samaria was. Isaiah says it: “the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

The capital of Ephraim is Samaria. So Aholah the elder, Samaria, is the northern kingdom of Ephraim. The two women, the daughters of one mother, are an allegory to depict the whoredoms we committed as a nation, and Aholah is the northern half of it.

precepts.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son.
precepts.point: Go, and do thou likewise. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here.

note.label: Luke 10: The Seventy Sent and the Good Samaritan

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.” Samaria was the head of Ephraim, so the Samaritan who had compassion, bound up the man’s wounds, and paid for his keeping was of the northern kingdom.

The priest and the Levite who passed by on the other side were both of the southern kingdom, and neither had mercy on their own. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here: “Go, and do thou likewise.”

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and the head of Ephraim is Samaria.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
Isaiah names the Samaritans: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

The head of Ephraim is Samaria. The Samaritans were Ephraim, the northern kingdom, and Ephraim was to be broken within threescore and five years, “that it be not a people.” That is the separation between the Jews, who were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and the Samaritans, who were Ephraim. It is written in the prophets.

precepts.text: The head of Syria is Damascus, which places Caesarea Philippi and the Syrophenician region under that rule.
precepts.point: Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why: “For the head of Syria is Damascus”. Damascus is the head of Syria, which places Caesarea Philippi and the Syrophenician region under that rule. Caesarea, where the brethren brought Saul down, sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus, and from there he was sent forth to Tarsus.

precepts.text: Because Syria, Ephraim, and Pekah took counsel against Judah, within threescore and five years Ephraim shall be broken that it be not a people.
precepts.point: Isaiah then prophesied that because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years so that it would be "not a people," and Hosea said the same, that Ephraim was joined to idols and would get no more mercy but be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria. Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture, and heritage and were assimilated into the nations.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Isaiah prophesied against that conspiracy: “Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying, Let us go up against Judah, and vex it”, “Thus saith the Lord God, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.”

“For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

Because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years, “that it be not a people.” Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture and heritage and were assimilated into the nations. That is how the northern kingdom became “another nation.”
